_comment: pi-system Control API — CONFIG / INTEGRATION REGISTRY (the allowlist).
This file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for which .env keys the Control API is
allowed to read and write. It is an ALLOWLIST: the API can ONLY ever touch a key
that appears here — never an arbitrary .env variable. Each key declares:
key             the exact .env variable name.
label           a human-friendly name for the web UI.
secret          true  -> the VALUE is never returned to the client (masked /
set / empty only) and never written to any log.
false -> a non-sensitive setting (its value MAY be shown).
service         the platform service this key belongs to (informational).
restart_services  which services must be RESTARTED for the change to take
effect. Each name MUST be in the bot-exec restart allowlist
(scripts/lib/bot-lib.sh BOT_VALID_SERVICE). [] = nothing to
restart (e.g. one-shot jobs that read env at run time, or
project-level credentials consumed on the next deploy).
validate        a basic SHAPE check applied before a value is written:
telegram_token | digits_csv | digits | enum | url | token |
text. (Independently, NO value may ever contain a newline —
the writer rejects that to prevent .env line injection.)
allow_empty     true -> the key may be cleared (disable an integration).
SECURITY: secret VALUES are NEVER returned by GET /api/integrations and NEVER
appear in the audit log. Editing init-time secrets that would corrupt an already
initialized datastore (e.g. a database password) is deliberately NOT offered here.

integrations.label: Telegram management bot
integrations.description: Operator-only bot that monitors/controls the platform from Telegram (runs as an n8n workflow through the audited bot-exec bridge).

keys.label: Bot token (from BotFather)
keys.note: HTTP API token from @BotFather. In n8n this is normally a Telegram credential; setting it here keeps .env in sync.

keys.label: Allowed Telegram user IDs
keys.note: Comma/space-separated NUMERIC ids permitted to command the bot. Empty = the bot authorizes no one (fail closed).

integrations.label: AI enrichment (SEO / prospects)
integrations.description: Optional, swappable AI provider used by the SEO auditor and prospect organizer. Off by default; both jobs are one-shot and read these at run time, so nothing needs restarting.

keys.label: AI provider
keys.note: Blank or 'none' keeps the engine FREE and rule-based (no network call is ever made).

keys.label: AI API key
keys.note: Your own API key. Usage is billed on your account. Required to enable AI enrichment.

integrations.label: Web analytics (Umami)
integrations.description: Self-hosted, privacy-first web analytics. Only the app secret is editable here; the dedicated database password is intentionally not exposed (rotating it would break the initialized store).

keys.label: Umami app secret
keys.note: Signs Umami auth tokens. Rotating it logs every Umami user out (no data loss). Restart the analytics service afterwards.

integrations.label: WhatsApp Business integration
integrations.description: Credentials for the (deferred) WhatsApp Business API integration used by generated projects. Consumed by a project on its next deploy, so no platform service needs restarting.

integrations.label: Local payments
integrations.description: Credentials for the (deferred) local payment gateway integration (e.g. Moyasar / mada / STC Pay) used by generated projects. Consumed by a project on its next deploy.
